description: Store a file to attach to an email later: up to 15 MB, sent as `content` (its bytes in base64) with its `name` and `type`. The answer holds its `id` and the `sha256` of the bytes we stored: compare it with your own to know the file arrived whole. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB, about 750 KB of file: for a bigger file call create_file_upload and PUT its bytes from a shell. The workspace keeps up to 1,024 MB of files in all, counting 15 MB for each upload URL not used yet; past that it answers 409 serverErrors.fileStorageFull. A file is kept while an unsent draft or a scheduled, reserved or sending email uses it, and deleted 7 days after it was stored or last used, or sooner with delete_file (409 serverErrors.filePinned while in use); reading or listing it doesn't change that. Attach up to 10 files by passing their ids as fileIds to create_draft, update_draft, draft_reply, reply_to_message or send_transactional_message.

content.description: The file's bytes, in base64. The file can be up to 15 MB. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB, so send about 750 KB of file at most there, or use create_file_upload to PUT the raw bytes from a shell.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name.description: The file's name, like invoice-1042.pdf, up to 255 characters. We take out control and invisible characters, slashes and double quotes, and keep the rest as you wrote it.

type.description: The file's type, like application/pdf or image/png. Left out, application/octet-stream. We keep what you say and never read the bytes to check it.

name: create_file
title: Store a file
